teacherNotes.title: 5-Step Vocab Progression
teacherNotes.content: 1. Recognition -> 2. Pronunciation -> 3. Classification -> 4. Controlled Production -> 5. Personalised Use

teacherNotes.title: Core Words
teacherNotes.content: hello, hi, goodbye, bye, good morning, good afternoon, good evening, teacher, student, classroom, book, listen, read, write, speak

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10-20 items):
hello, hi, goodbye, bye, good morning, good afternoon, good evening, teacher, student, classroom, book, listen, read, write, speak
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Hello, my name is... (introducing oneself)
• Nice to meet you (polite response)
• How are you? (social greeting)
• I'm fine, thank you (answering social greeting)
• Open your book, please (classroom instruction)
• Can you repeat, please? (classroom request)

teacherNotes.title: Phonetic Aim
teacherNotes.content: Alphabet Vowels & Word Stress: Short vowels /æ/ in 'cat', /e/ in 'pen', /ɪ/ in 'listen'. Falling intonation in greetings.

elements.content: Pronunciation Focus:
Alphabet Vowels & Word Stress: Short vowels /æ/ in 'cat', /e/ in 'pen', /ɪ/ in 'listen'. Falling intonation in greetings.

teacherNotes.title: Function-First Grammar Rule
teacherNotes.content: Subject Pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) + Verb 'be' affirmative (am, is, are). Use 'be' to state identity and role.

elements.content: Grammar System & Functional Framing:
Subject Pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) + Verb 'be' affirmative (am, is, are). Use 'be' to state identity and role.
Examples:

• I am a student.
• You are the teacher.
• He is Alex.
• She is Maria.
• We are in class.
Reading Dialogue & Script:

Script using target language:
Person A: Hello, my name is...
Person B: Nice to meet you
Listening Comprehension Prompt: Listen to the prompt and confirm understanding.

teacherNotes.title: Speaking Aim (~70%)
teacherNotes.content: Pair roleplay, information gap, and personalized speaking task.

elements.content: Communicative Speaking Task:
Practice with your partner: I can greet people, say goodbye, introduce myself, and use basic classroom language.
Short Writing Task (~10%): Write 3-4 sentences in your notebook applying target chunks.

teacherNotes.title: Multi-Duration Strategy
teacherNotes.content: Choose 60m, 90m, or 120m flow based on scheduled class length.

elements.content: Timestamped Multi-Duration Flows:

• 60 min Flow (Essential): 0-10m Warm-up & Goal; 10-25m Vocab & Classroom Language; 25-40m Grammar 'be' Affirmative; 40-55m Speaking Roleplay; 55-60m Cool-down & HW.

• 90 min Flow (Expanded): 0-10m Warm-up; 10-30m Vocab & 5-step drills; 30-50m Grammar & Substitution Drills; 50-70m Pair Roleplays; 70-85m Writing & Reading; 85-90m Cool-down.

• 120 min Flow (Full Workshop): 0-15m Warm-up & Icebreaker; 15-40m Vocab & Pronunciation Lab; 40-70m Grammar Workshop; 70-100m Group Classroom Simulation; 100-115m Portfolio Response; 115-120m Cool-down.

teacherNotes.title: Individual Adaptation
teacherNotes.content: Focus on 1-on-1 repetition, tailored error correction on /æ/ sound, personalized roleplay with teacher.

teacherNotes.title: Group Adaptation
teacherNotes.content: Pair speed-greeting drill, mingle activity where students collect 3 names and roles.
